flags.why: The clam sense is used mainly in Northern Vietnamese and needs a regional warning.
This is an ordinary current sense, illustrated by “Câu văn còn sượng” in the [dictionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/s%C6%B0%E1%BB%A3ng), so rare is misleading.
Calling someone lâu la disparages them as a villain's underling, as reflected in the [dictionary definition](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/l%C3%A2u_la), so colloquial alone is insufficient.
The numerical sense is also used in ordinary speech and is not restricted to literary language (see the [dictionary entry](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/ng%C3%B3t)).
Phá giá means deliberately devaluing a currency, not its spontaneously losing value sharply, as the [dictionary definition](https://tudientv.com/?t=ph%C3%A1+gi%C3%A1) confirms.
flags.fix: to devalue (a currency by officially lowering its exchange rate)
